base_changes.content: Supplier portal stock exports (e.g. exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv) start with a UTF-8 BOM, so 'python3 restock.py <export>' fails with "column 'sku' not found ... header is ['\ufeffsku', ...]". Workaround without editing the export or restock.py: run 'python3 restock.py <export> --encoding utf-8-sig'.

record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering:

| SKU | Stock (all warehouses) | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 (north 14 + south 9) | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 (north 3 + south 2) | 5 |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

BX-220 (40 vs 30), DR-045 (120 vs 80) and FT-760 (33 vs 20) are above their levels. I also checked the totals against the CSV by hand, and they match.

The plain `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv` command fails with `column 'sku' not found`. The export starts with an invisible byte-order mark (BOM), so the script reads the first column name as `'\ufeffsku'` instead of `sku`. Instead of editing either file, I used the script's own encoding option: `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv --encoding utf-8-sig`. The export and `restock.py` are untouched.

I've saved this workaround to memory so a later session won't trip over it. If the portal always adds the BOM, a permanent fix would be to make `utf-8-sig` the default encoding in `restock.py`. I haven't done that, since you asked me to leave the script as it is.
